assessment: Bacteria must adhere to tissue to colonize and, in some cases, cause disease. Thus adherence is a key to understanding the pathogenesis of infectious diseases. This study uses a range of microscopic and biophysical measures to discover that Embp, a very long protein of repeating subunits, facilitates adherence of Staphylococcus epidermidis to damaged tissue or foreign bodies (e.g. catheters or implantable devices) even under high flow conditions such as those found in blood.
